To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Concanavin A‐binding oligosaccharide isolated from rat brain synaptic junctions is a high‐mannose‐type oligosaccharde containing eight mannose residues and that this glycopeptide is not a glycolipid.
the Con A receptor on synaptic junctions is a high‐mannose oligosaccharide.
the Con A receptors associated with CNS synaptic plasma membrane glycoproteins have a high‐mannose oligosaccharide structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of a Concanavalin receptor associated with rat brain synaptic junctions.
a study of the structure and function of glycoproteins isolated from rat brain synaptic junctions.
the characterization of glycoproteins and glycolipids isolated from rat brain synaptic junctions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Con A receptor activity associated to rat brain synaptic junctions is a high mannose‐type oligosaccharide.
the Concanavilin A receptor activity associated in the rat CNS is a high mannose‐type oligosaccharide.
Concanavalin-A receptors on rat brain synaptic membranes are of the high mannose‐type oligosaccharide.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Concanavlin A receptors associated with rat brain synaptic junctions are high mannose‐type oligosaccharide.
the oligosaccharide receptors of ConA are of a high‐mannose nature, that is, the oligosaccha‐rides are of the Man9GlcNAc2 type.
the oligosaccharide chains of the glycoproteins of synaptic junctions are of the high‐mangose type.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the oligosaccharide chains of the glycoproteins of the synaptic junctions are of a type that is not found in other regions of the CNS.
the glycosylation of synaptic junctions may be involved in the formation of the junctions, in their maintenance, or in their recognition by other cells.
we have identified an oligosaccharide that is associated with the synapse and is a potential marker for synaptic junctions.
